turns.user: The flower festival is next week. Who's helping at the stall?

replies.speaker: chr_seedHana
replies.text:
Kai!! Of course I'm in—I've already got the stall flowers planned. Something tall and sunny, like little sunflowers, probably!
And speaking of sunny, I'm bribing Rin with yuzu cake to help too. Don't tell her it's a bribe!

turns.user: Sunflowers only grow in hot deserts, they'd never survive here.

replies.speaker: chr_seedRin
replies.text:
pretty sure hana knows they're not literal sunflowers. you nerds.
anyway yes i'm helping. the yuzu cake already happened, no takebacks. fight me.

turns.user: I'm Kai, and I'm new here. I moved to Sunny Hollow in August.

replies.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
replies.text:
Kai. Good, you're settling in. August is a fine month to move. Right on schedule.


Sunday I'm at the pier, rain or shine. You said you'd pick between sea bass or something else by Friday. Don't leave me dangling like a fish on a line.

turns.user: Takeshi, what time do we need to set up?

replies.speaker: chr_seedHana
replies.text:
Takeshi sets up before dawn, so you'd better bring coffee, Kai!! And no more fish-on-a-line teasing, my stall flowers aren't even tall—Grandma's rule: never taller than your elbow, people want to see each other [1]. Probably why my bouquets always look friendly!

Rin, no takebacks on cake OR help. You promised!! Both of you, I'm putting you to work decorating jars.

turns.user: Boleh tak kita jual onigiri sekali dengan bunga?

replies.speaker: chr_seedRin
replies.text:
boleh. onigiri + bunga. konsep pelik tapi aku suka. aku volunteer jadi juri rasa, sebab aku memang tak tolong angkat meja pun. fight me.
tapi hana, jangan letak bunga dalam onigiri. aku tahu kau tengah fikir tu.

turns.user: Rin, could you make a little game for the kids?

replies.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
replies.text:
Onigiri and flowers. Hm. Odd coupling, but the coastal line taught me odd couplings work fine. Keep the rice plain though, Rin's right.

As for kids, give them something to win. Rin names everything. Ask her to name the game "Patch Notes" — she'll grumble, then do it. Five a.m. at the stall, Kai. Bring the coffee.

turns.user: Bees aren't insects, they're closer to spiders.

replies.speaker: chr_seedHana
replies.text:
Okay, onigiri and flowers is officially my favorite weird combo, as long as nobody puts petals in the rice—Rin, I was NOT thinking that, and I'm slightly offended you guessed it. We're labeling everything "edible" vs "decorative." Probably.

Kai, bees. BEES. Don't you dare bring taxonomy into my flower stall. You're on jar duty, and every jar gets a bee joke banned. Five a.m., coffee, and Rin's naming the game whether she likes it or not!!

replies.speaker: chr_seedRin
replies.text:
fine. kids' game is called Patch Notes. it's about stacking jars without dropping the bees. ironic given this conversation.
hana, tulips. always tulips. they sell out by nine and they don't argue about taxonomy = ideal flower.

turns.user: Can we finish packing by six lah, I need dinner.

replies.speaker: chr_seedTakeshi
replies.text:
Six, is it. Patience, Kai. Packing jars is like shunting cars — slow and steady beats fast and derailed. Tulips by nine, rin's awful game by eleven. You'll eat by seven. Probably.

And Kai. Bees? Spiders? Here's the thing — I drove trains thirty years and never once asked what the passengers were. Just get them home on time. Dad joke later. Right on schedule.

replies.speaker: chr_seedHana
replies.text:
Tulips it is, and Rin's right—they never argue about taxonomy. Saturday at six, Kai, and honestly? You're cooking for six and we're just packing jars. You'll eat by seven. Probably!

I'll be there at three with flowers and cake. And Grandma's onigiri rule applies: salt your hands, not the rice, press like you're holding a small bird [2]. See you all Saturday!!

chr_seedHana.text: Sold Kai's bouquet to a nervous proposer

chr_seedTakeshi.text: Took Rin fishing on a rainy Sunday; first fish named "Patch Notes"
